data.title: Tree Select
data.tagline: Choose one or more items from a hierarchy
data.description: A tree selector fits departments, categories, and permission scopes with parent-child relationships. Explain whether selecting a parent includes its children, what a partial selection means, and which level is actually submitted.

avoid: Force flat data into a tree
Hide the meaning of partial selection
Load a huge tree without search or lazy loading
Submit a different level from the one the user sees

lessonPractice.title: An access scope must select several groups across departments and show partially selected parents. Which control fits?

options.label: Use a multi-select tree, define parent-child selection rules, and keep labels, partial states, and submitted nodes consistent
options.feedback: Correct. The task needs visible hierarchy and cross-branch selection, which a tree selector can express together.

options.label: Use a cascader that keeps only one path from the company to a single group
options.feedback: A cascader fits one path and cannot preserve groups selected under several departments.

options.label: Put every group in one flat dropdown and let the backend infer parent scopes
options.feedback: A flat list hides department relationships, and the backend cannot reliably infer rules the interface never expressed.

data.agentPrompt: Change “Visible data scope” to a multi-select tree selector. Selecting a department should select all of its child groups, while selecting only some children should show the parent as partially selected. After the panel closes, show selected scopes as labels and submit the real node IDs. Add search when the tree is large. Test expand and collapse, parent selection, clearing one child, cross-branch selection, search, and submission, and confirm the partial state, labels, and submitted values stay consistent.
